thesis: Linde reported Q3 2026 sales of $9.40B vs $8.62B a year earlier, affirmed its $1.60 quarterly dividend, and drew a Kepler Cheuvreux upgrade to Buy on Nov 19; the stock is up ~19% YTD and back above its 200-day average. That is offset by a $425M restructuring charge largely tied to the Lincare home-care unit, Erste Group cutting FY2027 EPS estimates, management saying it sees 'no catalyst' for an industrial rebound, and recent CFO/VP share sales. The evidence is mixed rather than a clear net read, which suggests continuing to hold but not adding conviction. No scheduled litigation event or 3-year governance failure was found.
invalidation: Q4 guidance cut, further restructuring charges, or price closing back below the 200-day moving average

thesis: Southern Co is up ~12% over 60 days, supported by Georgia large-load credits (worth at least $949M/yr for 2029-31) that Jefferies says could help avoid a base-rate increase, and it sits just above its 200-day average. However, on Nov 12, 2026 it announced a $1.75B equity-units offering, and it settled $1.2B of ATM equity in Q3 with ~$2B of further equity needs projected through 2030, which is a disclosed dilution source. A Georgia federal judge also let a pension class action proceed on Nov 9 (no scheduled next step found). With dilution and regulatory uncertainty around a reshaped Georgia PSC offsetting the load-growth story, this suggests only a low-conviction long.
invalidation: Georgia PSC moves to revisit rate design/ROE, or further equity issuance beyond plan

thesis: Home Depot reported Q3 FY2026 on Nov 17: sales $43.4B (+4.9%), adjusted EPS $3.86 vs $3.84 consensus, and U.S. comps +2.2%, and it raised revenue-growth guidance to ~4.5%. That was offset by gross margin contracting ~60bp, full-year adjusted EPS narrowed to ~$14.98 (below the $15.01 consensus) and comps guidance trimmed to ~1.4%; shares fell on the day. Longtime CFO Richard McPhail becomes CEO effective today after Ted Decker's medical leave — an internal succession not tied to execution problems, so not flagged. The stock is up ~16% over 60 days and back above its 200-day average. Results beating but guidance softening leaves the read mixed, which suggests only a low-conviction long. No scheduled litigation or governance failures were found.
invalidation: Further guidance cuts, comps turning negative, or price closing back below the 200-day average

thesis: Costco disclosed October (four weeks ended Nov 1) net sales of $24.50B, up 12.6%, with comparable sales up 7.3% ex-gas/FX and digital up 22.5%, and on Nov 10 declared a $30/share special dividend (record Nov 24) plus a reauthorized $4B buyback (8-K). These are confirmed company-disclosed results and capital returns. The strongest counter-case is valuation (~53x earnings) and the stock sitting ~2% below its 52-week high after a 23% 60-day run, which leaves less cushion; even so, the read holds because the advance is backed by accelerating reported comps rather than multiple expansion alone. The March 2026 consumer tariff-refund class action (N.D. Ill. 26-cv-02734) has no scheduled ruling or hearing found, and no governance failures were found. This suggests the holding thesis remains intact.
invalidation: Monthly comparable sales decelerate sharply (e.g., below ~4% ex-gas) or Q1 FY27 margin disappoints

thesis: P&G beat fiscal Q1 expectations with revenue up 4% to $23.28B and held its full-year outlook; it is up ~16% over 60 days and ~2% below its 52-week high, with Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and Citi raising targets after its investor day. Offsetting that, coverage flags a ~$1.4B commodity cost headwind and executive share sales (CFO sold 33,624 shares Nov 4), and the recent rally partly reflects defensive rotation during the market correction. The evidence is mixed rather than a clear net read, which suggests only a low-conviction long. No scheduled litigation or governance failures were found.
invalidation: Full-year outlook cut on commodity costs, or a rotation out of defensives reversing the 60-day move

thesis: Lilly reported Q3 2026 revenue up 39% to $24.4B on Oct 29 and raised full-year guidance; China approved its oral GLP-1 orforglipron (Foundayo) on Nov 12, ahead of Novo's oral Wegovy there, and Foundayo already contributed $184M in the quarter. The stock has pulled back ~7% from its Nov 13 high without a company-specific cause, alongside the broad market correction. Active litigation (Streck whistleblower case headed to jury, GLP-1 MDL 3094 with bellwethers 'projected mid-2026 through 2027') has no confirmed trial date within ~90 days in what was found, so it is not flagged, but the schedule could not be verified. Multiple supportive factors exist without the litigation timing fully resolved, which suggests continuing to hold at moderate conviction.
invalidation: Adverse MDL bellwether ruling/trial date set, a guidance cut, or Foundayo launch trajectory disappointing

thesis: Visa did not trip a Step 2 signal; today's +1.9% move tracks the broad market rebound (S&P 500 +4.7%) rather than company news, and no new company-specific catalyst was found this run. The stock sits ~7% below its 52-week high and well above its 200-day average. The DOJ debit-monopolization case remains in discovery with the discovery cutoff extended to Jan 29, 2027 and trial not expected before 2028 — a procedural deadline rather than a ruling, so not flagged, but noted. No governance failures were found. With the latest move macro-driven, this suggests holding without added conviction.
invalidation: Adverse ruling or settlement terms in the DOJ debit case, or a payments-volume slowdown in the next quarterly report

thesis: SK hynix ADRs jumped ~20% today in the sector-wide chip rebound after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, but remain ~44% below their 60-day-ago level and ~38% below the 52-week high. Company overhangs are unresolved: U.S. export licenses for its China plants remain held up, and in the DRAM price-fixing class action that survived dismissal, defendants' response is due Dec 7, 2026. Today's move is sector/sentiment-driven rather than a company-specific improvement, which suggests no clear entry until the overhangs resolve. The 2005 price-fixing plea falls outside the 3-year governance window.
invalidation: Export licenses granted and memory pricing stabilizes, with the ADR holding above prior support on company-specific news

thesis: Apple hit a record close above $350 on Nov 9 and trades ~3% below its 52-week high, but its Nov 3 guidance put December-quarter gross margin at 45-46%, below estimates, and the stock trades ~39x earnings. The Supreme Court has scheduled oral argument for Jan 11, 2027 on Apple's appeal of the Epic App Store contempt ruling — a scheduled hearing within ~90 days — and the DOJ antitrust case continues with no trial date found. The evidence is mixed (record highs vs. soft margin guide and a pending high-court hearing), which suggests holding without added conviction. No governance failures were found.
invalidation: Adverse Supreme Court outcome on App Store commissions or iPhone demand weakening in holiday-quarter data

thesis: SpaceX shares are down ~14% over 60 days and closed Nov 20 at $127.79, below the $135 IPO price, after falling on post-midterm worries about congressional oversight of its government contracts; today's ~4% bounce came with the broad market. Overhangs include likely Congressional investigation of Musk's influence and contracts, a Nov 2 watchdog lawsuit over the Pentagon's Project Meridian panel Musk leads, and an unconfirmed Bloomberg report of a possible Tesla merger as soon as December. With only ~113 real trading bars (trend filter skipped) and the moves largely sentiment/political-driven, this suggests no clear entry.
invalidation: Clarity on government-contract scrutiny or a confirmed transaction that resets valuation, with shares reclaiming the IPO price

thesis: AMD is down ~33% over 60 calendar days and fell 13.2% on Nov 20 after a Hunterbrook short report (its affiliated fund is short) alleged that Entity-Listed Chinese server maker IEIT Systems kept receiving newer AMD firmware; AMD says it complies with U.S. law and that the claims misrepresent its practices. Today's ~7% rebound tracks the sector-wide rally on Nvidia's CEO reinstatement. The allegation is unproven and no SEC or Commerce action against AMD was found, but the export-control question is unresolved and the price action is sentiment-driven, which suggests waiting rather than entering. No 3-year governance failures were found.
invalidation: Commerce/AMD clarification clears the IEIT allegation and the stock stabilizes on company-specific news

thesis: On Nov 22, 2026 Zscaler signed a definitive agreement (8-K/425) to be acquired by CrowdStrike in an all-stock deal at 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share (~$43.9B EV, a 34% premium to the Nov 20 close), with founder Jay Chaudhry's ~34% stake committed by voting agreement; the stock jumped ~18% on 7.7x average volume. From here ZS trades as a fixed-ratio proxy for CrowdStrike stock plus a merger spread, with closing not expected until the second half of CrowdStrike's FY2028 pending regulatory approvals — a long, approval-dependent timeline. A competing bid is the main counter-case, but the 34% voting commitment makes that unlikely. This suggests the short-term risk/reward for a new long is unattractive. No scheduled litigation or governance failures were found.
invalidation: Deal terminated or a higher competing bid emerges

thesis: CrowdStrike beat Q3 FY2027 estimates and raised guidance, but simultaneously announced an all-stock ~$43.9B acquisition of Zscaler, and shares fell ~9% on 4.5x average volume, now ~26% off recent highs. The deal implies substantial new share issuance (dilution) and a long integration/regulatory path to a close in 2H FY2028. Litigation: the shareholder suit over the 2024 outage was dismissed in Jan 2026, DOJ closed its distributor-deal probe in Sept 2026, and Delta's suit is in discovery with no trial date found. Strong operating results are offset by deal dilution and integration risk, leaving the read mixed, which suggests avoiding a new entry for now.
invalidation: Market re-rates the deal favorably (shares recover pre-announcement level) with confirmed accretion targets

thesis: BILL signed a definitive agreement on Nov 19, 2026 (8-K) to be taken private by TPG with Corpay at $63.25 per share in cash (~$6.0B), with Starboard and the CEO agreeing to vote in favor and closing expected in 1H 2027. At $61.59 the remaining upside is capped near the ~2.7% deal spread while a deal break would expose downside toward pre-rumor levels; the volume spike reflects deal-related repositioning rather than a new operating signal. A competing higher bid is the main counter-case, but none has been reported and the stock trades below the agreed price. This suggests the short-term risk/reward for a new long is unattractive. No shareholder suit with a scheduled hearing or governance failures were found.
invalidation: A competing higher bid emerges or the agreement is terminated/renegotiated

thesis: Best Buy traded 2.7x its average volume ahead of Q3 FY2027 results due before the open tomorrow (Nov 24), the first report under new CEO Jason Bonfig (planned succession announced in April amid stagnant sales). Consensus is ~$1.48-1.49 EPS on ~$9.9B revenue against company guidance of 1-3% comps, while Bank of America keeps a Sell on memory-cost pressure on margins and options imply a ~9.7% move. With an unresolved binary earnings event hours away, this suggests waiting for the actual results rather than entering beforehand. No scheduled litigation or governance failures were found.
invalidation: Q3 results and holiday guidance beat with margin intact, re-evaluated next cycle on the actual numbers
